provisions.description: Continuous, iterative risk management across full lifecycle including risk identification, estimation, evaluation, elimination/reduction/mitigation, residual risk acceptance, testing, and post-market monitoring integration

sub_provisions.description: Establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system consisting of a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle of a high-risk AI system
Identification and analysis of the known and the reasonably foreseeable risks that the high-risk AI system can pose to health, safety, or fundamental rights

provisions.retention_years_basis: INFERRED default, NOT stated by Art. 9 (which sets no retention period). The 10-year figure is reached transitively: Annex IV point 5 — 'A detailed description of the risk management system in accordance with Article 9'. The chain is: the named Annex IV point is content of the Art. 11 technical documentation ('The technical documentation ... shall contain, at a minimum, the elements set out in Annex IV'), and Art. 18(1)(a) puts a 10-year period on 'the technical documentation referred to in Article 11'. ANCHOR: the clock runs from placing on the market / putting into service, NOT from the evidence-record timestamp; a consumer computing an expiry date from record timestamps will compute it wrong. Art. 18(2) (Member State-defined arrangements applying on provider bankruptcy or cessation of activity) and Art. 18(3) (financial-institution providers redirected to Union financial services law) are out of scope for this profile and are not modelled. It is a profile choice about the transitive Annex IV -> Art. 11 -> Art. 18(1)(a) chain, not a citation of Art. 9.

provisions.description: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system, ensuring a level of traceability appropriate to the intended purpose

retention.basis: Art. 12 states NO retention period. It has exactly three paragraphs and imposes a system-level logging CAPABILITY duty only — Art. 12(1): 'High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system.' The phrase 'over the lifetime of the system' qualifies the recording capability, not any keeping duty. The previously published 10-year value was uncited and is WITHDRAWN: Art. 18(1) is a closed enumeration of five document classes and logs are not among them; Art. 16 splits the two duties into '(d) keep the documentation referred to in Article 18' and '(e) when under their control, keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems as referred to in Article 19'; and Annex IV does not include logs of the Art. 12(1) kind — it contains no reference to Article 12, and its only 'logs' are the point 2(g) development-phase test logs. The period that DOES attach to the Art. 12(1) logs is the at-least-six-months floor in Art. 19(1) (provider) and Art. 26(6) first subparagraph (deployer), modelled as the separate article-19 and article-26.6 provisions of this template and enforced there against the record-envelope /retention/min_retention_days field. Corrected per GitHub issue #1.

evaluation.message: At least one event_log record is required — Art. 12 mandates automatic recording of events throughout the system lifecycle

A logging_spec variant event_log record is recommended to document what the system logs and why, enabling deployers to interpret logs per Art. 12(1)

provisions.description: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs referred to in Article 12(1), automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months

retention.basis: EU AI Act Art. 19(1): Providers shall keep the logs referred to in Article 12(1), automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent such logs are under their control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in the applicable Union or national law, in particular in Union law on the protection of personal data. This is a MINIMUM FLOOR, unbounded above — not a fixed period — so it is not representable as an integer number of years, which is why retention_years is null here. Art. 19(2) routes providers that are financial institutions to their obligations under Union financial services law. The 10-year figure in Art. 18(1) governs documentation, not logs: Art. 16 splits the duties expressly into '(d) keep the documentation referred to in Article 18' and '(e) ... keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems as referred to in Article 19'.

At least one event_log must declare retention of >= 180 days — the 'at least six months' floor binding the provider

adoption.basis: Art. 113 third paragraph point (c), as replaced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Art. 1 point (40)(b): Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2 December 2027 for systems classified as high-risk under Art. 6(2) and Annex III, and from 2 August 2028 for systems classified as high-risk under Art. 6(1) and Annex I. Arts. 19 and 26 are both Chapter III Section 3. ACEF cannot express the Annex I / Annex III discriminator (effective_date is a single value and the risk_classification enum in the frozen v1 manifest schema has no such value), so effective_date carries the EARLIER limb as a conservative projection and both limbs are recorded here. A consumer MUST NOT read effective_date alone as a definitive statement that the obligation applies to a given subject between 2027-12-02 and 2028-08-02.

provisions.description: Providers of AI systems that generate synthetic audio, image, video, or text content shall ensure that the outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated

retention.basis: CITED: no paragraph of Art. 50 states any keeping or retention duration. Art. 50(2) requires that providers of AI systems generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content 'shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated'; Art. 50(1)-(7) were read in full and none of them attaches a period to any record. No retention obligation is asserted by this profile for this provision. This is a determination that the instrument states no period — it is distinct from 'not assessed'. Any retention duty over transparency-marking evidence must be sourced elsewhere (for a high-risk system that also falls under Chapter III, Art. 18(1)(a) may reach the marking description as Annex IV technical-documentation content; that chain is not asserted here).

evaluation.message: At least one transparency_marking record is required — Art. 50(2) mandates machine-readable marking of synthetic content
Every transparency_marking record must specify marking_scheme_id — the marking standard or scheme used must be identifiable for interoperability verification
Every transparency_marking record must specify the content modality (text, image, audio, video, multimodal) for which marking is applied
Transparency marking records should specify the metadata_container used (e.g., C2PA manifest, EXIF, ID3) per Art. 50(2) interoperability requirements

provisions.description: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall provide technical documentation, a copyright policy compliant with Directive (EU) 2019/790, and a sufficiently detailed training data summary

retention.normative_text_ref: EU AI Act Art. 53(1)-(7), Annex XI Sections 1-2
retention.basis: CITED: no paragraph of Art. 53 states any keeping or retention duration. Art. 53(1)(a) requires the provider of a general-purpose AI model to 'draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation, which shall contain, at a minimum, the information set out in Annex XI'; 'keep up-to-date' is a currency duty, not a keeping-period duty. Art. 53(1)-(7) and Annex XI Sections 1-2 were read in full: Annex XI specifies documentation CONTENT only and states no period. Note that Art. 54(3)(b) does place a 10-year keeping duty on the GPAI provider's AUTHORISED REPRESENTATIVE ('keep a copy of the authorisation ... at the disposal of the AI Office for a period of 10 years'); that duty binds a duty-holder this profile does not model and is therefore not asserted as this provision's retention. This is a determination that the instrument states no period for the provider — it is distinct from 'not assessed'.

evaluation.message: GPAI models must document training data provenance — Art. 53(1)(d) requires a sufficiently detailed summary of training data
GPAI models must document copyright compliance — Art. 53(1)(c) requires a policy to comply with EU copyright law including TDM opt-out mechanisms

A gpai_annex_xi_model_doc variant evaluation_report is recommended — Annex XI requires structured technical documentation including model architecture, training data characteristics, and compute resources
Data provenance records must specify source_type (licensed, scraped, public_domain, synthetic, user_generated) per Art. 53 training data summary requirements
